content:
- Overestimate prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon when sentiment is negative or mildly bearish (e.g., sentiment < 0.0), especially after recent spikes.
- Underestimate late-period price surges (last 5–7 days of forecast) when sentiment turns positive or shows momentum (e.g., sentiment > 0.0 or rising), particularly if true outcome exceeds forecast by >5%.
- Apply mean reversion correction: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Lag correction: if true outcome is >10% above forecast on day 10–15, adjust forecast for days 16–30 by subtracting 0.5–1.0% per day to avoid overcorrection.
- Overshoot after spikes: if forecast peaks >15% above recent high, reduce peak by 2–3% and flatten slope for next 3 days.
- Sentiment-driven bias: if sentiment > 0.1 for 3+ consecutive days, shift forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% per day; if sentiment < -0.2, shift downward by 0.5–1.5% per day.
